out: The record of the experiments your coding agents run, as Rabbit Brain YAML files in your repo: questions, experiments with their hypothesis, variants and criteria, runs with receipts, and the resources they used. Agents record; rb checks and computes findings; you decide. Documentation: rb docs. New here? Run rb tour.
question     add|move|reword: what the work is trying to find out, as a tree experiments are filed under
experiment   add|file|relate|gate: what is tested: its purpose, hypothesis, variants and settings; where it is filed; how it stands to others; the decision it gates
variant      add: an arm of an experiment: baseline, candidate, control, ablation
note         add: words about an experiment or the project: an assumption, a caveat, context; a note changes no finding
metric       add: the catalogue: a metric's unit, which way is better, its other names
spec         set|verify|vary: an experiment's settings, where each value comes from, and whether rb has checked it
criterion    add|file|relate: a rule over one comparison, declared before the evidence it reads
run          add: what ran: its results, per-run settings, inputs and outputs, with a receipt
analysis     add: a computation over saved outputs, and the comparisons it produced with their intervals
resource     add|locate|expose: a dataset, checkpoint, code or artifact: what it is, where its bytes are, how to get it again, who has looked at it
freeze       lock an experiment's spec and criteria before the evidence, recorded with who locked it

decide       a call on a criterion, an experiment, a question or a setting: accept, reject, investigate; continue, park, stop, pivot, ship. Recorded with who made it and why; in an agent session it is proposed until the user confirms it
confirm      make a call proposed, or a past call mentioned, in an agent session yours, or an experiment's design one wrote: run in your own terminal; with no id, list what waits
retract      take anything back: it stays on record, stops counting, and rb says what rested on it
open         the catalogue in your browser, live and read-only, on 127.0.0.1 only
ui           open this project in your terminal: your call, the cards, the tree (bare rb does this too)
status       each criterion on its axes, and what is open, with who usually acts
show         one record: a criterion with its finding, an experiment with its spec, a run with its receipt, e1/lr with its history; or a .yaml record file as canonical JSON
compare      an experiment's own table: variants by metrics, with changes against the baseline
log          every write, newest last: who, how, what
context      the record as one Markdown briefing a fresh agent session reads first
page         write the project as one self-contained, read-only HTML file you can send anywhere
export       write the project's page with a hashed manifest, readable without rb; with --with-record, the record too, as a portable bundle
clone        start your own line of work from an exported bundle: the structure arrives inherited, and nothing counts until reproduced here
env          the environment: check this machine against the record's runs and any env.* settings
mcp          serve the record to an agent over MCP (stdio); every call is recorded as the agent's
skill        print the agent skill; `rb skill add` installs it for your coding agent
journal      what rb observed in the repository: files that appeared, git moves, wrapped commands
reconcile    compile the repository against the record: each results folder with a report as an experiment, what its files say (verbatim), its checks, how to reproduce it; --apply keeps it
compile      list what existing reports and results files the record can place, and what it cannot; writes nothing
doctor       check the record: who you are recorded as, edits made outside rb, merge leftovers, sources outside the repository
fmt          write Rabbit Brain YAML files in their canonical form, comments kept (default: every record file under .rb/)
telemetry    optional usage analytics: off until you enable it; never sends research content
config       rb's own settings on this machine: whether rb keeps itself up to date
remove       take rb out of this checkout: only what checks out as rb's (the record, its instructions for agents, its pages and exports, its refs and folders in git), after showing the plan
tour         a one-minute walkthrough: builds a small real project in ./rb-tour and runs the whole loop
docs         print AGENTS.md (--start: how to start the record in a project already under way; --errors: the error table)
schema       print a JSON Schema: `rb schema all` is Rabbit Brain format 1 (rb-v1.schema.json), `rb schema <kind>` one record's shape
feedback     a link to send feedback on rb: the page shows what it would send before you send it; rb sends nothing
login        rabbitbrain.ai, optional: sign this machine in with a short code, approved on any device where you are signed in
logout       revoke this machine's hub credential and remove it from the credentials file
sync         rabbitbrain.ai, optional: a private copy of this record's page in your account, for your own eyes from anywhere
rb <command> --help for its arguments. Start: rb init "<the work's theme>", then rb question add for each question the work asks, and rb context.
